c.tagline: A perfectly preserved Ming and Qing old town of purple pottery, ancient wells and China's second-largest Confucius Temple.

taxi.fareNote: Didi is by far the easiest way to book a car; the old town is largely pedestrian, so cars drop you at the gates. Metered street taxis exist but drivers often prefer a negotiated flat rate for trips out to Twin Dragon Bridge or Tuanshan.

emergency.note: 120 is the ambulance number, 119 is fire and 110 is police. English is rarely spoken, so a translation app or your destination written in Chinese helps a lot.

hood_desc: The living heart of old Jianshui (historically called Lin'an), centred on Lin'an Road and the imposing Chaoyang Tower gate, a lattice of stone lanes, courtyard mansions, ancient wells and purple-pottery workshops; the most atmospheric and walkable base, buzzing with local snack stalls after dark.

The quieter western quarter around the vast Confucius Temple - the second-largest in China after Qufu - and the old Xuezheng imperial examination hall, fronted by the reed-fringed Xuehai (Sea of Learning) pond; a calmer, culture-heavy pocket a few minutes' walk from the main street.

The lanes around the elaborate Zhu Family Garden, a sprawling Qing-era merchant compound of linked courtyards, ponds and ancestral halls now partly run as a heritage guesthouse; a central, atmospheric spot surrounded by boutique inns in old residences.

Modern Jianshui east of the walls, with the railway station, long-distance bus station, chain hotels, supermarkets and everyday services; less charming but the practical, convenient base for transport and cheaper rooms.

The rural southeast fringe toward the seventeen-arch Twin Dragon Bridge over the Lu and Tachong rivers and, further out, the well-preserved traditional village of Tuanshan - the terminus of the historic narrow-gauge tourist railway; a scenic, slow-paced area for those wanting countryside and photography.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:30 AM to 8:30 PM; after that use Didi or a taxi, especially between the old town and the railway station in the new town.
transit.note: Jianshui has no metro; getting around means city buses, Didi, taxis and plenty of walking, as the compact old town is best explored on foot. Buses and Didi link the old town, the new town, the railway station and out to Twin Dragon Bridge and Tuanshan.
transit.pay: Pay city buses in exact-change cash or, more commonly, by scanning with Alipay or WeChat Pay; foreign visitors should set up mobile pay in advance, as it is now the default.

transit.m: Fast train from Kunming to Jianshui Railway Station (~2.5-3 hr), then a local bus or Didi into the old town
Intercity coach from Kunming South Bus Station to Jianshui (~3-4 hr)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in mainland China and is generally not expected in restaurants, taxis or hotels.
